gumtree_entries.description: ADDED i1: Tests that the TimedSemaphore builder accepts chained configuration calls (setTimeUnit, setService, setLimit, setPeriod) and that the built semaphore can start
ADDED i2: ---- Build the TimedSemaphore via the builder ----
ADDED i3: Start with a fresh builder and pin the time unit to HOURS
ADDED i4: Create a first executor backed by a mock factory that returns null threads. This executor has 0 core threads, so submitting a task exercises the rejection / thr
ADDED i5: Build a four-deep chain of mock threads and submit the leaf to the executor
ADDED i6: Wire the first executor into the builder and disable the permit cap (limit = 0)
ADDED i7: Repeat setLimit(0) to confirm idempotent behaviour, then replace the executor with a larger one (2780 core threads) backed by a second null-thread factory
ADDED i8: Set an invalid period of 0 first, then override it with 2780 before building. Because all builder setters return `this`, the last call wins at get() time.
ADDED i9: ---- Construct the semaphore and exercise post-build behaviour ----
ADDED i10: Changing the builder after construction should not affect the already-built semaphore
ADDED i11: Start the internal timer task on the executor, then read state that is always available without acquiring (acquireCount = 0 initially, period = 2780)
